A.explanation: At $I = 0.5\text{ A}$, $V_P \approx 2.0\text{ V}$ and $V_Q \approx 4.0\text{ V}$, so $P = IV$ gives about $1.0\text{ W}$ in P and $2.0\text{ W}$ in Q.

B.explanation: At $I \approx 1.9\text{ A}$ both curves meet near $V \approx 7.5\text{ V}$, so $R = V/I$ is almost the same for P and Q, not half.

C.explanation: For an $I$-$V$ graph $R = V/I = 1/\text{gradient}$, and the gradient of Q gets steeper with current, so its resistance decreases.

D.explanation: P is straight through the origin so is ohmic, but Q bends upwards with increasing gradient so its resistance falls, opposite to a filament lamp where heating increases resistance.

hints: Draw a horizontal line at $I = 0.5\text{ A}$ across the $I$-$V$ graph and read the $V$ value where it meets curve P and where it meets curve Q.
Remember that at the same current, $P = IV$ means power is directly proportional to $V$, and $R = V/I$ means resistance is directly proportional to $V$.
For the shape, compare the $I$-$V$ gradient $I/V$ of Q at low and high $V$ and use $R = V/I$ to decide if resistance rises or falls.
walkthrough: Note the axes: $I/\text{A}$ is vertical and $V/\text{V}$ is horizontal, so resistance is $R = V/I$ and power is $P = IV$. P is a straight line through the origin, Q is a curve that starts flat and gets steeper.
Draw a horizontal line at $I = 0.5\text{ A}$. It meets P at $V_P \approx 2.0\text{ V}$ and meets Q at $V_Q \approx 4.0\text{ V}$.
Calculate power at this common current: $P_P = IV_P \approx 0.5 \times 2.0 = 1.0\text{ W}$ and $P_Q = IV_Q \approx 0.5 \times 4.0 = 2.0\text{ W}$.

So $P_Q$ is double $P_P$ at $0.5\text{ A}$. The other statements fail because at $1.9\text{ A}$ both have similar $V$, Q has increasing $I$-$V$ gradient so decreasing $R$, and a filament lamp should increase in $R$ with current.
